secfoo — AI security review CLI

 
 Turn the coding agent you already have into a disciplined security reviewer. 
 SAST, secret scanning, SCA, threat modeling and architecture review, with your design docs, Confluence and tickets as context. 
 Same checklist, same report shape, every run.
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 Website ·
 Getting started ·
 CLI ·
 CI guide ·
 Sample output 
 

 

That is the whole first run. No config file: secfoo picks the agent you
already have on PATH (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot, Cursor,
Antigravity, OpenCode, ...) or, if none is installed, uses the
 OPENAI API KEY / ANTHROPIC API KEY / GEMINI API KEY already in your
shell. Pass --agent to choose. Keep it around with pipx install secfoo 
or pip install secfoo ; more channels under Install.

 Context, not just code

A code repository is one input. Real reviews also need the design doc, the
threat model from last year, the runbook and the ticket that explains why the
odd thing is there. secfoo passes that context to the agent through
MCP and asks the skills to use it:
the architecture review compares what is documented (the provided
documentation sources, README, ADRs) with what is implemented and reports
the gaps; secret scanning covers linked documentation sources as well as code;
every report ends with a coverage section that says which documentation sources
were reached and which were not.

 

Connect remote documentation sources once in /.secfoo/config.toml ; any MCP
server works, so the same applies to SharePoint and Microsoft 365, Jira,
Notion, Google Docs or an internal wiki:

 

 Context How it gets in Used by 
 --- --- --- 
 Documentation sources (Confluence, Jira, SharePoint, Notion, Google Docs, local PDF/DOCX/Markdown) --context (repeatable; --confluence / -c alias) with an MCP server or local file extraction Architecture review, threat modeling, secret scanning, compliance skills 
 Jira, SharePoint, Notion, Google Drive, internal wikis [[mcp servers]] in config; the agent calls them as tools during the review Every skill 
 Vendor documents (PDF, DOCX, PPTX) and AI-BOM files secfoo assessment upload Third-party risk assessment, Responsible AI compliance 
 Curated vulnerability patterns secfoo memory signup (optional hosted service, exposed as an MCP server) SAST, SCA, secret scanning 

With --agent claude the configured servers are attached to each run
automatically and nothing else (your global Claude config is not touched and
the target's own .mcp.json is not loaded). For Gemini CLI and Cursor run
 secfoo mcp sync --agent once. Codex, Antigravity and the api 
agent cannot use MCP servers yet. Details in
docs/REFERENCE.md.

 A 30-second look at the dashboard

Everything a run produces lands in a local dashboard: secfoo serve , on your machine.

 
 
 

 Watch as MP4 

 
 
 
 

Screenshots are from a real local secfoo serve against public vulnerable-app targets.

 What you get

- A skill is a brief, not a parser. secfoo hands your coding agent a
 structured prompt and a target, then collects a report in a fixed shape.
- One dashboard for the program. Coverage, dispositions, STRIDE,
 design verdicts, and findings across every project you have scanned.
- Context-aware. Confluence pages, tickets, design docs and uploaded
 vendor documents reach the agent through MCP, and the report says which
 sources it could and could not read. See Context, not just code.
- Local first. Runs and secfoo serve stay on your machine. Optional
 secfoo cloud login syncs to an org portal that is not in this repo.
- Concurrent by default. Several --skill flags run at the same time.
- Portable findings. Export SAST, SCA, and secret-scanning findings as
 JSON Lines or SARIF 2.1.0 for GitHub code scanning and IDEs. See
 export examples.
- CI-ready. --fail-on high , --max-cost 2.00 , --json , and distinct
 exit codes for "the scan broke" vs "policy failed". Details in
 docs/CI.md.

 Activity catalog

 Activity Skill ID 
 --- --- 
 Security Architecture Review security-architecture-review 
 Threat Modeling threat-modeling 
 SAST — Static Code Analysis sast 
 SCA — Reachability & Upgrade Triage sca-reachability 
 Secret Scanning secret-scanning 
 Prompt Review prompt-review 
 Deployment Readiness deployment-readiness 
 Responsible AI Compliance responsible-ai-compliance 
 Third-Party Risk Assessment third-party-risk-assessment 

Run one, or several together. What each report actually contains is in
docs/REFERENCE.md. Write your own skill as a
Markdown file: docs/SKILLS.md.

 Agents

Point Claude Code, Cursor, Antigravity, Gemini CLI, Codex, Copilot, Droid,
Devin or OpenCode at a target with --agent , or use an API key with the
built-in api agent. Setup and troubleshooting for every adapter:
docs/agents.md. Choose a model for one run with
 --model , or set a per-agent default in
configuration.

 Repository targets

 --target accepts local directories, GitHub URLs, GitLab (including nested
namespaces), and Bitbucket Cloud repositories:

 

GitLab and Bitbucket support HTTPS and git@host:namespace/repo.git SSH URLs;
 .git is optional. SSH uses your existing SSH authentication. For self-hosted
GitLab, set SECFOO GITLAB HOST to its hostname, optionally with an HTTPS port
(e.g. git.example.org:8443 ), then pass that host's repository URL. The default
 gitlab.com remains supported. URL credentials, queries, fragments, HTTP, and
 ssh:// forms are rejected for these new targets.

For private HTTPS repositories, provide SECFOO GITLAB TOKEN (a GitLab token
with repository read access) or SECFOO BITBUCKET TOKEN (a Bitbucket repository,
project, or workspace access token with repository read permission) through your
environment or CI secret store. Bitbucket user API tokens/app passwords are not
supported by this token mode. Tokens are supplied to Git through a temporary
askpass helper, never placed in clone arguments, repository URLs, reports, or
Git config. Git errors omit raw server output to keep credentials out of logs.

install.title: Install
install.html:
uvx secfoo --help                     # run from PyPI without installing (uv)
pipx install secfoo                   # isolated install, Python 3.10+
pip install secfoo                    # PyPI
npm install -g @rakfortltd/secfoo     # npm, no Python needed
docker run --rm ghcr.io/secfoo-com/secfoo --help

No agent CLI? Use an API key:

export OPENAI_API_KEY=...             # or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / GEMINI_API_KEY
secfoo run --skill sast --target https://github.com/org/repo   # picks the api agent

Universal install scripts, standalone binaries, CI flags, spend tracking, and configuration live in docs/REFERENCE.md. Developing this repo: pip install -e ".[dev]".
